description.narrative: Gender Equality and Women´s Empowerment76. Based on a gender analysis (Attachment 5b), the project developed a Gender Action Plan (Attachment 5a). This plan incorporates relevant measures and actions for the project to contribute to reducing gender gaps in the management of the páramos, which contribute on the one hand to addressing the risks associated with gender inequities, and on the other hand to enhance the opportunities identified for the benefits of the project for women and young people. understanding the reality of the populations involved, and achieving impact especially in three major gender outcomes:A. Reduce gender gaps in access to and control of natural resources.B. Increase the participation and influence of women and youth in decision-making on natural resources (with special attention to women and youth from indigenous peoples and local communities).C. Generate socio-economic benefits and services for women and youth (with special attention to women and youth from indigenous peoples and local communities).77. To achieve these results, the project applies the following principles of gender equity throughout the project: 1. Differentiated indicators: to the extent possible, the project includes differentiated indicators in all project framework outcomes.2. Specific training: the four strategic components of the project include specific training to include the gender dimension in technical activities and strategies (e.g. restoration, land use, access to finance, governance, research and communication).3. Empowerment of women, youth and other traditionally disadvantaged groups: in the different components of the project, affirmative measures of women's participation are applied, and the aim is to specifically benefit them and other disadvantaged groups (youth, indigenous people, rural poor).4. Communication and monitoring of gender equity and social inclusion: the project differentiates its communications to diverse audiences, targeting inclusion and avoiding exclusionary or negative language towards specific groups. Also, the project seeks to actively communicate its activities and achievements in terms of equity and inclusion.5. Gender equity in the project work team: a balanced work team is sought without negative discrimination towards gender, ethnicity and age. The participation of women in decision-making positions is promoted. Strict safety principles are applied in the workplace (against discrimination and harassment at work). 6. Rights-based approach: the entire project is designed and implemented under a human rights-based approach, which also determines aspects of gender equity. To this end, the Gender Action Plan is complemented with other tools that institutionalize the rights-based approach, such as the application of social and environmental safeguards and the social and environmental management plan (Annex F), the stakeholder engagement plan (Annex F and Attachment 5c) and the grievance and redress mechanism (Annex F and Attachment 5d). 78. In this line, the main gender measures and actions to be implemented in the project are presented, organized in the Gender Action Plan according to the components of the project. The total specific budget is $173,500, but there are additional funds included in other project activities that are necessary to achieve the project's gender outcomes. Stakeholder Engagement 79. A stakeholder engagement plan, including resources required, is presented in Annex F and Attachment 5c and uploaded to the portal.Private SectorWill there be private sector engagement in the project? The National Action Plan (PAN) for the páramos was constructed in a participatory manner; local communities were consulted through seven meetings during the design phase and again, during socialization. NGOs, academies and international agencies were invited to a national workshop. During this process, the idea of a GEF project as a potential way to initiate implementation of the PAN was communicated. 81. During PIF development, all directions of MAATE were consulted in a workshop on 12 September 2023. Potential partners (GIZ, CONDESAN, FAO, FONAG, Ecopar, USFQ, FIAS, KfW, CI, TNC) were consulted individually at the start of PIF development (early September) and were invited to a workshop were the main elements of PIF were presented and discussed, roles agreed and indicative cofinancing confirmed (27 September 2023). During PPG, frequent meetings were held with the Biodiversity directorate staff of the MAATE to discuss progress of the PPG phase and agree on the different activities. The potential project partners were convened again on May 8, 2024, to present the PPG process and request their recommendations and define synergies with ongoing work. During PPG, several meetings were held with local stakeholders in the intervention areas, to agree on the final areas and partners. These were assisted by MAATE staff, local governments, NGO and communities (see Stakeholder engagement, Annex F and Attachment 5e). On December 2024, a final presentation of the final project design was made by MAATE and CI to project partners. The project includes a specific component on knowledge management, that will complete knowledge gaps on páramo management, develop maps and GIS system, an information management system and a monitoring system, connected to existing knowledge systems. The knowledge management system has several audiences:· Páramo management agencies at national and local level (MAATE, MAG; local governmental agencies, protected areas management) will be provided with general and fit-for-purpose knowledge on páramo diversity, management, governance and financing. Also, the monitoring system will show them the effectiveness of the management applied.· MAATE provides the planning and feedback hub for processes of Common Country Analyses (CCAs) and UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks (UNSDCFs e.g. UNDAF), including updates for results as well as future planning as these frameworks roll out new versions.· Local land user communities will be provided with local environmental, social and financial knowledge to support their activities to sustainably use, conserve and restore páramo areas and to enhance their wellbeing· Agencies promoting páramo conservation and sustainable management (NGO, development partners, CSO) will obtain science-based information to better target current and future initiatives · The research community will have access to frontline páramo knowledge as baseline information for developing further research· The general public in Ecuador will profit from communication campaigns to increase awareness on the importance of páramo and ways to support its conservation. 83. In addition, as part of project's component 5 (project management and evaluation) the project execution will be continuously monitored according to the indicators of its results framework are reported upon to the project management unit and the steering committee. Output indicators are concrete and achievement or not can be immediately converted into lessons that can inform the adaptive management of the project’s execution. The project will receive two external independent evaluations: a mid-term review and a terminal evaluation. 84.
